```{r setup}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# State Scorecard — branded, paginated "Download" report
#
# Rendered on demand by the Shiny app's download_state handler in
# ADA_PARC.Rmd, with the same params (state_abbr, year, palette, contrast)
# the reader selected on screen. This document does NOT recompute scores: it
# calls build_state_scorecard() in state_scorecard_core.R, the same function
# state_scorecard.qmd (the on-screen version) calls, so the two can never
# report different numbers for the same state. See the header comment in
# state_scorecard_core.R.
#
# What IS unique to this document: the ADA-PARC brand masthead and grant
# funding footer, and the print/pagination CSS below. Those intentionally
# stay out of state_scorecard_core.R and out of state_scorecard.qmd — the
# on-screen version runs inside the Shiny app's own navbar chrome and never
# needs a masthead, and per the National Data download's own precedent, a
# report type's banner/footer is hand-written for that report rather than
# shared, so different downloadable products can diverge independently.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
options(cli.width = 80)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(out.width = "100%", dpi = 96, fig.retina = 2)

library(htmltools)

local({
  cand <- c("state_scorecard_core.R",
            file.path("scorecard", "state_scorecard_core.R"))
  hit  <- cand[file.exists(cand)]
  if (length(hit) == 0) {
    stop("state_scorecard_print.qmd cannot locate state_scorecard_core.R. ",
         "Render with execute_dir set to the scorecard/ directory, ",
         "or from the project root.")
  }
  source(hit[1], local = FALSE)
})

ctx <- build_state_scorecard(
  state_abbr = params$state_abbr,
  year       = params$year,
  palette    = params$palette,
  contrast   = params$contrast
)
# invisible() matters here: list2env() returns the environment it just
# populated (this chunk's own environment == R_GlobalEnv when this document
# is rendered from the Shiny app's download handler), and as the last
# expression in the chunk it would otherwise auto-print. That auto-print is
# exactly the stray "<environment: R_GlobalEnv>" line that used to appear
# above the masthead on every rendered scorecard.
invisible(list2env(ctx, environment()))
```

```{css}
/* ── Brand masthead + funding footer ─────────────────────────────────────
   Not part of scorecard_state.css: the on-screen scorecard sits inside the
   Shiny app's own navbar and never shows a masthead, so these classes exist
   only here. Colour tokens are the fixed ADA-PARC brand maroon/gold, NOT the
   reader's chosen palette/contrast — the masthead is the organization's
   identity, not a data encoding, so it does not change with Display
   settings the way tier colours on the page below it do. */
:root {
  --adaparc-maroon: #6d1f2e;
  --adaparc-gold:   #c9a84c;
}

.adaparc-banner {
  background: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  color: #ffffff;
  border-bottom: 5px solid var(--adaparc-gold);
  padding: 1rem 1.25rem;
  margin: 0 0 1rem 0;
}
.adaparc-banner .banner-content {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 0.75rem;
  max-width: 8.7in;
  margin: 0 auto;
}
.adaparc-banner .banner-icon { height: 2.2rem; width: auto; flex-shrink: 0; }
.adaparc-banner .brand {
  font-size: 1.6rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  letter-spacing: 0.03em;
  margin: 0;
  font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
}
.adaparc-banner .sub {
  font-size: 1.05rem;
  font-weight: 500;
  margin: 0.15rem 0 0 0;
  color: #f3e6c9;
  font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
}

.adaparc-footer {
  max-width: 8.7in;
  margin: 1.5rem auto 0 auto;
  padding: 0.75rem 1.25rem 1.5rem;
  border-top: 2px solid var(--adaparc-gold);
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  color: #555;
  font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
}
.adaparc-footer p { margin: 0.2rem 0; }
.adaparc-footer .funding-note { font-weight: 600; color: #1c2b3a; }

/* ── Screen-only print control ────────────────────────────────────────────
   Hidden in print via the @media print rule below, so it never appears in
   a saved PDF. */
.print-bar {
  max-width: 8.7in;
  margin: 0 auto 1rem auto;
  padding: 0 1.25rem;
}
.btn-print {
  font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
  font-size: 1.02rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: #ffffff;
  background: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  border: 1.5px solid var(--adaparc-maroon);
  border-radius: 6px;
  padding: 8px 18px;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.btn-print:hover  { background: #8b2737; border-color: #8b2737; }
.btn-print:focus  { outline: 3px solid var(--adaparc-gold); outline-offset: 2px; }

.print-hint {
  font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
  font-size: 0.92rem;
  color: #555;
  margin: 0.5rem 0 0;
}

/* ── Pagination ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   An explicit page box gives print/PDF engines a defined page size so
   forced breaks are actually honoured (without @page, some "save to PDF"
   paths lay the whole document on one continuous page). See
   feedback_quarto_print_pagination memory / national_topic.qmd for the full
   write-up of why this is necessary. */
@page {
  size: Letter;
  margin: 0.6in 0.5in;
}
.print-page-break {
  break-before: page;
  page-break-before: always;
}

@media print {
  /* Quarto wraps the document in #quarto-content.page-columns, a CSS grid,
     with main.content as a grid item. Chromium does not fragment grid
     containers, so without this the whole document prints as one clipped
     page and every break-before rule below is silently ignored. */
  #quarto-content,
  #quarto-content.page-columns,
  .page-columns,
  main.content,
  main#quarto-document-content,
  .cell {
    display: block !important;
    grid-template-columns: none !important;
  }

  /* The blanket ".cell { display: block !important; }" above fixes Chromium's
     refusal to fragment a CSS grid container across pages, but it also
     stomps scorecard_state.css's own
       .banner-ranks > .cell,
       .banner-ranks > .cell > .cell-output-display { display: contents; }
     which is what keeps the four rank pills as direct flex children of
     .banner-ranks. Losing "contents" here turned each pill's Quarto wrapper
     into a full-width block, so the four pills that should sit in one row
     stacked as four tall cards instead, spilling the banner across two
     pages before a single domain card had even started. Restate "contents"
     for just this wrapper, after the blanket rule, so it wins on source
     order at equal specificity. */
  .banner-ranks > .cell,
  .banner-ranks > .cell > .cell-output-display {
    display: contents !important;
  }

  .print-bar { display: none !important; }

  body { font-size: 11.5pt; }

  /* Backgrounds carry meaning here (masthead, tier chips, sub-index bar
     fills, summary table header/stripes), so ask the engine to print them
     rather than drop them. */
  body,
  .adaparc-banner {
    -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact;
    print-color-adjust: exact;
  }

  .adaparc-banner  { padding: 0.6rem 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.7rem; }
  .adaparc-banner .banner-icon { height: 26px; }

  .adaparc-footer {
    break-inside: avoid;
    /* Was 8pt. Bumped to keep the funding note above ~9.5pt printed, in
       line with the project's accessibility minimum-font-size bar — 8pt
       reads uncomfortably small on paper even for a footer, which sits
       oddly on a disability-rights research center's own deliverable. */
    font-size: 9.5pt;
    margin-top: 0.6rem;
    padding-top: 0.4rem;
  }
  .adaparc-footer p { margin: 0.1rem 0; }

  /* Each domain card and the summary table are the units a reader reasons
     about; none should straddle a page break. This is already the rule
     on-screen (see scorecard_state.css's own @media print block, which
     still applies here too since this document links that stylesheet); it
     is restated with the .print-page-break hook so the Score Summary table
     always opens a fresh page rather than starting a few lines from the
     bottom of one. Page budgeting (whether CL+CP fit together on page one,
     for instance) has not been measured against an actual print preview
     yet — that needs one round of visual QA against a real render. */
  .domain-card, .summary-table-card, .about-category {
    break-inside: avoid;
    page-break-inside: avoid;
  }

  a[href]:after { content: ""; }
}
```

```{r doc-tokens, results='asis'}
# Same :root token block the on-screen scorecard emits, from the same
# palette/contrast this render used. See the fuller note in
# state_scorecard.qmd's own doc-tokens chunk.
cat(doc_header_html)
```

```{r banner, results='asis'}
cat(paste0(
  '<div class="adaparc-banner">',
  '<div class="banner-content">',
  '<div>',
  '<p class="brand">ADA-PARC</p>',
  '<p class="sub">State Scorecard &nbsp;·&nbsp; ',
  htmltools::htmlEscape(state_name), ' &nbsp;·&nbsp; ',
  htmltools::htmlEscape(as.character(year_label)), ' Data</p>',
  '</div>',
  # Same white knockout mark used on the National Data and fact sheet
  # download banners. Decorative (alt=""): the adjacent "ADA-PARC" text
  # already names the organization for screen readers.
  '<img class="banner-icon" src="../www/brand/PARC_white_icon_knockout.png" alt="">',
  '</div>',
  '</div>\n'
))

cat(paste0(
  '<div class="print-bar">',
  '<button type="button" class="btn-print" onclick="window.print()">',
  'Print or save as PDF</button>',
  # Chrome/Edge/Firefox print dialogs default "Headers and footers" ON,
  # which stamps the browser tab title, local file path, timestamp, and a
  # generic page count across every page of an otherwise branded document.
  # CSS cannot suppress that (it is dialog UI, not page content), so this
  # is a one-line nudge to turn it off rather than a silent gap.
  '<p class="print-hint">For a clean copy, turn off &ldquo;Headers and ',
  'footers&rdquo; in the print dialog’s More settings before saving.</p>',
  '</div>\n'
))
```

```{r}
    "Housing Access"

  state_scores = c(s("index_rel_living_arrangements"),
                   s("index_rel_community_resource"),
                   s("index_rel_housing_access")),

)))
```

```{r funding-footer, results='asis'}
# Same funding acknowledgment wording used on the National Data and City
# Data downloads (see the equivalent chunk in national_topic.qmd /
# city_profile.qmd) and on the fact sheets. Kept as a literal string per
# document, per the existing convention of not sharing a banner/footer
# component across report types.
cat(paste0(
  '<div class="adaparc-footer">',
  '<p class="funding-note">The ADA-PARC is funded by the National ',
  'Institute for Disability, Independent Living, and Rehabilitation ',
  'Research (NIDILRR) under grants 90DP0026 and 90DPAD0001.</p>',
  '<p>ADA-PARC &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; ADA Participation Action Research Consortium &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; ',
  'Generated ', format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y"), '.</p>',
  '</div>'
))
```
